subject: Help with the code to calculate basking and foraging duration, the body temperature and body mass, and why body mass lowers trough the time period

messages.author: 7b9976a7166ab661
messages.subject: Help with the code to calculate basking and foraging duration, the body temperature and body mass, and why body mass lowers trough the time period
parts:
Hello, good afternoon. I hope everyone is well.

I am kindly requesting help in resolving three questions. After running the shared code (below and in the attached file), there are two exercises to reproduce what I found (lines 266 and 273).

First, if I understand well the introductory vignette to the ectotherm subroutine, the duration of basking activity occurs when the simulated animal presents a body temperature framed between T_B_min and T_F_min, duration of foraging activity between T_F_min and T_F_max, total duration of activity between T_B_min and T_F_max (i.e., adding the duration of basking and foraging), and duration of inactivity out from the interval between T_B_min and T_F_max. I got these measurements automatically and by hand by using NicheMapR. I found that the daily hours of activity and inactivity calculated automatically equaled those calculated by hand. However, I also found that the daily hours of basking and foraging calculate automatically differed from those calculated by hand. Therefore, I would like to know if I made a mistake or if the basking and foraging duration are calculated with respect to parameters other than T_B_min, T_F_min, and T_F_max. That is, what is the code in NicheMapR to calculate the duration of basking and foraging? Note: Please run the code until the line 271 to reproduce the example regarding this first question.

Second, when I plot the body mass of simulated Sceloporus.undulatus along the days of the study period, I saw that the body mass lowered trough time. I repeated this with Sceloporus.occidentalis and Eulamprus.quoyii founding the same relationship. Do you have an idea of why this relationship is happening even with different species? Note: Please, run the line 275 to reproduce the example regarding this second question, then please change the species name in the line 12 of the R script, and run again the code.

Third, although the theoretical basis for calculating body temperature and body mass is explained in the articles and vignettes related to NicheMapR, I have not been able to find the code in NicheMapR specific to calculate both variables. So, I would be grateful if you could provide me with the name of the articles or vignettes where such codes are reported.

Thank you very much for your attention and help.

--

messages.subject: Re: Help with the code to calculate basking and foraging duration, the body temperature and body mass, and why body mass lowers trough the time period
parts:
Hi Israel,

For question 1, you are manually counting times that Tb is within certain limits but not checking to see if it is nighttime / dusk and the animal is diurnal - I suspect that's the problem.
For question 2, you have redefined parameters after getting the parameters out of the allstat list. The result is that your specified initial conditions for structure and reserve density are higher than what they should be and the animal heads down towards the steady state. You shouldn't change the parameters from those you get out of allstat.
For question 3, did you see the recent message I sent about ectoR_devel? That has all the code to compute Tb. It finds the heat fluxes for all the different heat exchange mechanisms, (QSOLAR, QIRIN, QMET, QIROUT, QCONV, etc.), and then iteratively guesses the Tb that balances the heat budget. For the DEB theory, wet mass is calculated based on the current values of structure, reserve, reproduction buffer and stomach contents. The code is in the ectotherm Fortran code but also in the R DEB functions in NicheMapR, e.g. the code:
  wetgonad <- ((E_R / mu_E) * w_E) / d_Egg + ((E_B / mu_E) * w_E) / d_Egg
  wetstorage <- ((V * E / mu_E) * w_E) / d_E
  wetgut <- ((E_s / mu_E) * w_E) / fdry
  wetmass <- V * andens_deb + wetgonad + wetstorage + wetgut

which is lines 737-740 in DEB_euler
https://github.com/mrke/NicheMapR/blob/master/R/DEB_euler.R

Hope that helps.

All the best,
Mike
